news.Title: Target has a problem that sends shoppers to Amazon
news.Content:
Target has always been my retail destination of choice, but I don't even have its app on my phone. That's because if I need something quickly, I go to Amazon.

If I need something only available from Target and I need it fast, I'll place my order on Uber Eats, even though it will often cost more than buying it in-store.

It's a weakness for the retail giant, as it's losing sales to Amazon and Walmart because those retailers offer next-day, and in some cases, same-day delivery.

That's an area where Target has been quietly investing in an effort to bridge the gap with its rivals.

Target improves its delivery

While Target has never been top-of-mind for me when it comes to delivery, the chain has been expanding its reach.

"Over 60% of the U.S. population has access to quicker, easier shopping as Target expands next-day delivery of online orders to more markets. Guests in more than 50 top U.S. metro areas will be able to get their purchases delivered next day — in many cases for free. It's yet another option among Target's fulfillment offerings, which also includes guest-favorite same-day services and two-day shipping," the chain shared in a press release .

Target owns Shipt , which offers free same-day delivery on orders over $35. It also offers a $99 annual membership that waives those limits.

More Target:

Target tackles a frustrating problem for shoppers

Target jumps on food trend Kroger and Publix embraced

Target rolls out another generous deal to win back customers

The chain has also expanded its selection of items available for delivery.

"Most items eligible for shipping at Target are eligible for next-day delivery. That includes hundreds of thousands of items — 85% of what we sell in Target stores," the chain shared.

Next-day delivery is free for orders over $35 or with no minimum order amount if you're a Target Circle 360 member or use your Target Circle Card for purchases.

"This is just one of the ways Target offers a convenient digital shopping experience. We already reach 80% of the U.S. population with same-day delivery — often within two or three hours — and 99% with two-day shipping. And our Order Pickup and Drive Up services are always free and available for guests on their timeline," Target shared.

Target needs to fix delivery

Target has a big bridge to cross in order to catch up to its rivals.

Walmart already serves nearly the entire country with same-day service.

"We expanded our U.S. store-fulfilled delivery areas in Q4 FY25. We can now reach 93% of U.S. households with same-day delivery," the company shared in its fourth-quarter 2025 earnings release .

Story Continues

That number climbed to 95%, according to an April press release .

eMarketer analyst Rachel Wolff warned in April that Target faces a difficult path to catching up with Amazon and Walmart on delivery speed.

"Target's delivery speed disadvantage underscores how difficult it is to catch up as Amazon and Walmart are zooming ahead. At this point, it's unclear whether Target has the means — or even the vision — to close the gaps with its competitors.

"Much of the company's turnaround strategy is rooted in returning to its pre-pandemic model, rather than reinventing the business for an age in which customer loyalty is more fragile and more spending is shifting online," she wrote.

Target tries to catch up to Amazon and Walmart

RTM Nexus CEO Dominick Miserandino had a simple response when I asked him about Target investing in delivery.

"They need to! They're the go to for that quick purchase and that feeling of getting it asap is the consumer standard," he told TheStreet.

Target COO Lisa Roath talked about delivery during the chain's second-quarter earnings call .

"We also saw meaningful gains in delivery speed. This past quarter, we fulfilled nearly 30% more same-day and next-day units than last year, and we will continue investing to get even faster," she said.

Delivery, she noted, is part of a broader effort to improve customer service.

"When we combine the impact of our in-store transitions, assortment changes, tech enhancements and improvements in inventory reliability, it all adds up to an elevated experience that is being noticed by our guests," she added.

Those efforts, Roath shared, have started to pay off.

"Overall satisfaction scores continue to improve across multiple measures of the guest experience, extending the momentum we shared with you last quarter and reinforcing that our continued investments in our teams, training and our team's tireless execution are making a difference," the COO said.

The chain has been addressing concerns that GlobalData Managing Director Neil Saunders raised in September ahead of Michael Fiddelke taking over as CEO.

"Visiting Target stores is less pleasurable and less fun than it used to be," Saunders said in an email. "There is far too much friction, and the experience is sometimes unpleasant. That's an issue as it lowers the probability of people making visits, reduces visit frequency, and weakens conversion and basket size when people are in stores," he told Retail Dive .

Related: Walmart gets aggressive when it comes to holiday sales

news.Title: Will Alphabet Stock Surge After Oct. 28?
news.Content:
Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG)(NASDAQ: GOOGL) reports Q3 2026 earnings after the market closes on Oct. 28. Wall Street analysts have an average revenue estimate of $127.8 billion, which would be a 25% year-over-year increase, and earnings per share (EPS) of $3.

Last quarter, Alphabet easily surpassed revenue expectations -- and its share price still ended up falling 7% the next day. Based on the tech giant's recent track record, investors probably shouldn't feel too confident about which direction Alphabet stock will move immediately post-earnings.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

What history says about Alphabet's post-earnings performance

The way Alphabet stock moves after an earnings report is about as predictable as a coin flip. Over the last four quarters, it has had an even split, closing higher the day after earnings twice and closing lower twice, despite beating headline EPS expectations each time. Its moves this year have been significant, closing up 10% after its April 29 report, and down 7.1% after its July 22 report.

Stretching it to the last 16 quarters, Alphabet has closed up seven times and closed down nine times. The average move is 5.2% in either direction.

Why July's beat turned into a sharp drop

Alphabet's earnings report in Q2 2026 looked great on the surface. Revenue was up 24% to $119.8 billion, Google Cloud revenue grew 82% to $24.8 billion, and EPS skyrocketed 294% to $9.11. The company's post-earnings slump makes more sense when you dig a little deeper.

Net income included about $99 billion in unrealized gains, mostly from Alphabet's investments in Space Exploration Technologies and Anthropic, and that caused the huge jump in EPS. These holdings are certainly valuable, but an increase in unrealized gains is much different from an increase in sales. Alphabet's adjusted EPS (without the unrealized gains) was $2.85, which actually missed consensus estimates by $0.04.

Alphabet also raised its 2026 capex guidance to between $195 billion and $205 billion, and management said that 2027 capex will increase significantly. The company ended the quarter with negative free cash flow for the first time in its history since going public in 2004. The heavy spending worried investors and resulted in a sell-off.

What to watch on Oct. 28

Story Continues

There are a few potential swing factors, outside of revenue and EPS, to watch for in Alphabet's Q3 earnings. Any updates to its 2026 capex, as well as early guidance for 2027, could cause a big move, especially as rates have gone up and investors have become increasingly concerned with AI spending.

Free cash flow will give an idea of how manageable Alphabet's spending is. CFO Anat Ashkenazi said it will "remain under pressure" in the Q2 earnings call. How deep in the red it ends up will likely play a role in how the market reacts to earnings. Finally, Google Cloud revenue is a key metric, as it indicates that all the AI spending is turning into measurable sales growth. Ideally, Google Cloud growth will hold around 80%.

All that said, it's best to keep your expectations open. Earnings reports and post-earnings performance are inherently unpredictable. Considering how investors have rotated out of AI stocks recently, I think a decline in Alphabet stock is more likely than a surge post-earnings. However, when you're a long-term investor, what matters is what a company does over a period of years, not right after earnings.

news.Title: Lumentum stock surges 10% as AI components ‘completely sold out’
news.Content: Lumentum Holdings (LITE) shares jumped about 8% to $818 on Monday, Oct. 26, after StoneX initiated coverage of the optical networking company with a Buy rating and a $1,200 price target. The rally spread to other optical networking stocks. Coherent (COHR) and Applied Optoelectronics (AAOI) gained about 6% and 7%, respectively, while the Roundhill Photonics & Optics ETF (LYTE) rose 4%. StoneX said Lumentum occupies "critical scarcity points" in high-speed indium phosphide lasers, cloud transceivers and optical circuit switches, The Fly reported . The analyst also highlighted management's comments that AI-related optoelectronic components were "completely sold out" through 2029, as Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston told Bloomberg earlier this month. The new price target implies roughly 47% upside from Lumentum's afternoon trading price. Why Wall Street is bullish on Lumentum Lumentum, based in San Jose, California, makes lasers and optical components used in telecommunications networks and data centers. The company has benefited largely from the AI infrastructure boom as tech hyperscalers spend billions of dollars building data centers that require faster connections between servers. Related: Analysts revamp Super Micro stock price targets after 10% surge on revenue boost One of its biggest backers is Nvidia (NVDA). In March, Nvidia announced a multi-year strategic partnership with Lumentum to develop advanced optical technologies for next-generation AI infrastructure. The agreement includes a multibillion-dollar purchase commitment from Nvidia and rights to access future manufacturing capacity for advanced laser components. Nvidia also committed to invest $2 billion in Lumentum to support research and development and expand U.S. manufacturing, including a new fabrication facility. "Together with Lumentum, NVIDIA is advancing the world's most sophisticated silicon photonics to build the next generation of gigawatt-scale AI factories," Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said in the announcement . StoneX isn't the only firm optimistic about Lumentum. On Oct. 20, Jefferies analyst Blayne Curtis raised his price target on Lumentum to $1,250 from $1,200 and maintained a Buy rating. Curtis expects Lumentum to capture a larger share of Alphabet's (GOOGL) optical circuit switching demand and benefit from growing adoption of 1.6T transceivers. Jefferies also expects Lumentum to become Alphabet's largest optical circuit switch supplier next year, overtaking the tech giant's in-house production. Lumentum earnings reflect growing AI demand Story Continues Lumentum's latest quarterly results showed strong demand for its optical networking products. In its fiscal fourth quarter ended June 27, the company reported revenue of $1.01 billion, up 109.3% from $480.7 million a year earlier. Adjusted earnings rose to $3.23 per share from $0.88 a year earlier. For fiscal 2026, revenue reached $3.01 billion, compared with $1.6 billion in fiscal 2025. Also read: Meta stock falls despite Wall Street analysts raising price targets The company expects fiscal first-quarter 2027 revenue of $1.225 billion to $1.275 billion, with adjusted earnings of $4.05 to $4.35 per share. Lumentum is scheduled to report its next quarterly results on Nov. 5. Investors will be watching closely whether the company can expand production quickly enough to meet demand, as well as its outlook for cloud networking revenue and profit margins. Lumentum shares have gained 122% so far in 2026, as of this writing, although the stock has pulled back sharply from its recent all-time high of $1,143, reached on October 8. news.Title: Stock Market Today, Oct. 26: AI Optimism Lifts Nasdaq as Tech Stocks Rebound
news.Content:
The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) gained 0.70% to 7,677, the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) rose 0.82% to 26,169 as AI optimism returned, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJINDICES:^DJI) edged up 0.28% to 52,362, diverging from Friday's energy-driven session as oil prices retreated.

Gold prices rose 0.46% to $4,026.30 as of U.S. market close and the 10-Year Treasury yield rose 0.04% to 5%, with investors favoring Real Estate and Technology stocks while Communication Services shares faced selling pressure.

Today's biggest moves

Surgery Partners (NASDAQ:SGRY) soared 48% on reports of a majority-stake takeover negotiation, while Lumentum (NASDAQ:LITE) jumped 8% following a bullish price target initiation. Conversely, Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) fell 2% after filing to raise capital for AI infrastructure, and Petrobras (NYSE:PBR) plunged 14% following election results in Brazil.

What this means for investors

The big driver for Wall Street's tech stock rally on Oct. 26, 2026 was the long-awaited initial public offering (IPO) filing by artificial intelligence giant Anthropic. The company filed its S-1 prospectus to go public on the Nasdaq under the ticker "ANT." Its massive revenue growth figures in the filing calmed investor fears that the artificial intelligence boom was losing steam.

Anthropic's IPO revived enthusiasm for technology stocks, helping the Nasdaq Composite lead the market today despite pressure on more mature communication services providers. Adding to today's market performance was Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) stock gaining over 5%. Barclays upgraded shares to an Overweight rating, and raised its price target from $370 to $450 due to potential ties with CEO Elon Musk's other company, SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX), growth in Tesla's robotaxi business, and a recovery in its core automotive operations.

Meanwhile, Meta Platforms shares slipped after the company disclosed plans to raise up to $95 billion for AI infrastructure, signaling that the immense capital requirements for industry dominance remain a primary concern for mega-cap investors. Next, investors are looking ahead to this week's earnings from Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) and the upcoming Federal Reserve interest rate decision, which will determine if the current momentum can survive tightening financial conditions.

news.Title: Don't Miss This Week's 5 Most Important Earnings Charts
news.Content:
Earnings season picks up steam this week with hundreds of S&P 500 companies reporting earnings including several of the Magnificent 7 stocks like Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon.

The AI Revolution trade will also be in the spotlight with several key infrastructure companies reporting earnings.

But it's not just about technology this week. Big pharma, key restaurants like Wingstop, Chipotle and Starbucks, and big oil like ExxonMobil and Chevron will also report earnings.

True Earnings All-Stars

These are five of the top earnings charts this week. They are true earnings all-stars. These companies have excellent earnings surprise track records and some of the stocks are trading near all-time highs.

It's not easy to beat every quarter, or nearly every quarter, for several years in a row.

Can they beat again?

5 of the Most Important Earnings Charts This Week

1. Vertiv Holdings Co. ( VRT )

Vertiv has an excellent earnings surprise track record. It has only missed twice in the last 5 years and the last miss was in 2023.

Shares of Vertiv are down 21% over the last month as the AI trade has weakened. It's gotten more attractive on its valuation with a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) of just 28.9.

With the bears in charge, will another beat even matter right now for Vertiv and the other AI stocks?

2. Microsoft Corp. ( MSFT )

Microsoft has an excellent earnings surprise record with just one miss in the last five years. That miss was all the way back in 2022.

Shares of Microsoft are up 3.2% in the last month, bucking the technology stock weakness. It's back to trading near its all-time highs.

Will Microsoft beat again this quarter?

3. Eli Lilly & Co. ( LLY )

Eli Lilly has strung together five earnings surprises in a row. The shares are up 8% in the last month and are trading near all-time highs.

Eli Lilly isn't cheap. It trades with a forward P/E of 38 but you are buying the earnings growth which is expected to be up 37% in 2026.

Is it too late to get into Eli Lilly?

4. Sandisk Corp. ( SNDK )

Sandisk is an earnings all-star. It hasn't missed on earnings since it was spun off from Western Digital in 2025.

Shares of Sandisk have fallen 29% over the last month on the fears over the AI slowdown. It is now dirt cheap. Sandisk trades with a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) of just 5.8. A P/E ratio under 10 means a company is a deep value.

Will another Sandisk beat even matter for the stock?

5. Alphabet Inc. ( GOOGL )

Alphabet has an excellent earnings track record. It hasn't missed since the AI Revolution began in 2023.

Story Continues

Shares of Alphabet are down 7.8% in the last month. Alphabet is cheaper than every with a forward P/E of 15.6. That's near a historic low for the company.

Will Alphabet beat again this quarter?

news.Title: KLA Corporation (KLAC) vs. AMAT and LRCX: Can Rising Semiconductor Complexity Create Another Growth Cycle?
news.Content:
Is KLAC a good stock to buy? We came across a bullish thesis on KLA Corporation on Astute Optics - US's Substack. In this article, we will summarize the bulls' thesis on KLAC. KLA Corporation's share was trading at $145.61 as of October 23rd 2026. KLAC's trailing and forward P/E were 39.78 and 26.95 respectively according to Yahoo Finance.

This isn't the first time we see a semiconductor equipment company pitched as a great investment. KLAC shares gained 19.83% over the last 12 months. Comparable stocks like Applied Materials and Lam Research gained 63.07% and 46.65%, respectively, during the same period. Why are semiconductor equipment stocks rising, and does KLAC's recent weakness make this a good time to buy?

Posonskyi Andrey/Shutterstock.com

In June, we published an article about the 10 Best Growth Stocks to Buy According to Billionaire Dan Loeb and KLAC ranked #8 in that article. KLAC has declined since then, leaving investors who backed the stock waiting for that confidence to translate into returns. This article explains why hedge funds were bullish on KLAC. Before getting into our analysis, let's take a look at the business and why some investors like the stock so much.

KLA Corporation (NASDAQ:KLAC) provides tools that help chip makers find defects, measure wafer quality, and run their factories more efficiently. Its fastest-growing opportunity right now is tied to artificial intelligence-driven semiconductor demand, and that is central to understanding the stock. As chips become smaller and more complex, manufacturers need more advanced inspection and measurement tools to keep production yields high, which is exactly where KLA Corporation operates.

Read More: 15 AI Stocks That Are Quietly Making Investors Rich

Read More: Undervalued AI Stock Poised For Massive Gains: 10000% Upside Potential

In fiscal 2026, the company's revenue reached $13.6 billion, up 11.7% from a year earlier, and it kept very healthy profit margins. These are strong results, but the stock is not cheap, as it trades at about 49 times trailing earnings and 33 times forward earnings. This suggests investors are paying not just for today's performance, but also for several more years of AI-related growth.

The positive case rests on KLA Corporation being a leader in process control, meaning the tools that catch problems during chip making. Every new generation of advanced chips needs more inspection and measurement, and even tiny defects can hurt production yields. As AI pushes chip makers to expand capacity and invest in newer manufacturing technology, demand for KLA Corporation systems should benefit. The company also enjoys long relationships with leading chip makers, who find it costly and difficult to switch suppliers. Growth in advanced packaging and AI-related chip investment could support the business for years.

Story Continues

The company's recent results support this view. KLA Corporation turned a large share of its sales into real cash, generating $4.14 billion in operating cash flow and $3.8 billion in free cash flow in fiscal 2026. Its 35.6% net margin and 76.1% return on equity show how efficiently it makes money for shareholders. Fourth-quarter revenue of $3.66 billion also came in above the midpoint of management's guidance, showing steady execution even in a choppy industry. If AI-driven chip spending continues and manufacturers keep adding advanced capacity, bulls believe the company can keep growing earnings and justify its premium price.

Analysts are also fairly upbeat. Their average price target of about $233.77 implies nearly 29% upside from the current price of roughly $180.64, with individual targets ranging from $175 to $325. This bullish outlook depends on continued AI-related chip investment, strength in advanced packaging, and stable margins. However, because the stock already carries a high valuation, slower earnings growth or weaker chip spending could make that price harder to defend. You can check out why Jim Cramer recommends buying KLA stock in small doses here .

A slowdown in chip industry spending is the main risk. Even if AI demand stays strong, semiconductor equipment is a cyclical business that depends on customers' investment decisions. Wider U.S. export limits on selling chip equipment to China add another challenge, since China has historically been a meaningful source of revenue for KLA Corporation. With a premium valuation and little room for error, the stock could come under pressure if growth slows, margins shrink, or geopolitical restrictions tighten.

Another risk for the stock is that rising chip complexity makes KLA's own product development harder and more expensive. Each new manufacturing process requires inspection tools that can detect smaller defects accurately without slowing production. KLA warns that its success depends on anticipating customer needs and launching new technologies on time and at competitive costs. Existing customer relationships cannot guarantee it wins every new equipment purchase. A delayed launch or a better competing tool could cost it business even while AI investment remains strong. Higher development spending could also pressure margins before new products generate revenue. In our opinion, this execution risk could pressure KLA's valuation if growing inspection demand fails to translate into sustained earnings growth.

Hedge fund positioning shows a mixed signal. As per our database, 81 hedge fund portfolios held KLA Corporation at the end of the second quarter, up from 71 in the previous quarter. That is a steady climb, suggesting institutional interest in the company is improving. Among its peers, Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT) was held by 137 hedge funds, down from 138, while Onto Innovation (NASDAQ:ONTO) was held by 75 hedge funds, up from 67, and Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX) was held by 139 hedge funds, up from 123. This shows institutional investors grew most confident in Lam Research Corporation during the quarter, with KLA Corporation and Onto Innovation also seeing solid gains, while Applied Materials held roughly steady with only a marginal dip in ownership.

Short interest data also paints a fairly calm picture, with just 1.86% of KLA Corporation shares sold short. That compares with 1.71% for Applied Materials, Inc., 2.07% for Lam Research Corporation, and a much higher 7.68% for Onto Innovation Inc. Because fewer investors are betting against KLA Corporation than Onto Innovation Inc., there is little direct bearish pressure on the stock. Still, its premium valuation and reliance on continued chip spending remain the key things to watch.

Valuation Analysis

KLAC's forward P/E is 26.95x. Applied Materials, Inc., Lam Research Corporation, and Onto Innovation Inc. trade at forward P/Es of 21.14x, 24.88x, and 16.84x, respectively. KLAC's own forward P/E was 33.44x on December 31, 2025, meaning its current valuation is approximately 19% lower. We believe the current valuation reflects investor concerns about semiconductor spending cycles, export restrictions, and the durability of AI-driven equipment demand. However, its premium to all three peers suggests that the historical decline has reduced expectations without making the shares an obvious bargain. KLA's fiscal 2026 revenue increased 11.7% to $13.6 billion, while fourth-quarter adjusted earnings per share rose approximately 12% from $0.94 to $1.05, supported by annual free cash flow of $3.77 billion. We believe continued earnings growth could support the current valuation, but a narrowing premium would reduce shareholder returns even if profits keep rising. If KLA can convert increasing chip complexity and advanced packaging demand into sustained earnings and cash flow growth, the shares could offer attractive long-term returns, although we would prefer a lower entry price to provide more protection against a slower semiconductor spending cycle.

Previously, we covered a bullish thesis on KLA Corporation (KLAC) by Quality Equities in January 2025, which highlighted semiconductor tailwinds, TSMC's capex expansion, and AI-driven demand for KLA's process control tools. KLAC's stock price has appreciated by approximately 94.19% since our coverage. We believe KLAC could be a good long-term investment at a lower price, as its premium valuation could limit returns even if earnings continue growing, particularly if semiconductor spending slows.

news.Title: Lumentum Is Sold Out Until 2029. Is LITE Stock Still a Buy at $800+?
news.Content:
Lumentum (LITE) is sold out of optical components through early 2029, according to CEO Michael Hurlston. Hurlston said the company could not meet about 70% of demand for certain products through 2027. In my view, Lumentum does not need to prove that artificial intelligence (AI) networking demand exists. It needs to produce enough components to serve that demand.

Lumentum's main advantage is that it sits on a scarce input: The lasers that power AI data-center optics. Its electro-absorption modulated lasers (EMLs) are in a supply crunch, helping the company with pricing power and margin expansion. This supply shortage also spreads across the company's continuous wave and ultra-high-power lasers. The best part about Lumentum is that demand for its lasers will seemingly always be there, whether the industry moves toward pluggable modules, near-packaged optics, or co-packaged optics.

More News from Barchart

How to Play RKLB Stock as Rocket Lab Pushes Its Neutron Launch to Next Year

Morgan Stanley Sees Amazon Stock Surging 100% with AWS Hitting $1 Trillion in Revenue Sooner Than People Think

Alphabet Stock: 3 Reasons Why GOOGL Is a Buy Ahead of Q3 Results

Tired of missing midday reversals? The FREE Barchart Brief newsletter keeps you in the know. Sign up now!

Released on Aug. 11, Lumentum's fiscal fourth-quarter results show how the company is already benefiting. Revenue surged 109% year-over-year (YOY) to $1.01 billion in Q4, while non-GAAP operating margin rose to 36.6% from 15% a year earlier. Management also guided Q1 fiscal 2027 revenue to $1.225 billion to $1.275 billion. This shows that the company is benefiting from both higher sales and improved efficiency. If Lumentum expands production without a similar increase in operating costs, the company could boost profits. Moreover, its 1.6T transceivers and optical circuit switching products offer additional growth opportunities.

About Lumentum Stock

Lumentum provides optical and photonic products, from components like lasers to systems spanning cloud transceivers and optical circuit switches. In recent years, the firm has become a crucial backbone of the global AI boom. Founded in 2015, the company is headquartered in San Jose, California.

LITE stock has soared in 2026, up 122% year-to-date (YTD) as investors have poured into companies benefiting from surging AI infrastructure spending. The bull rally has been led by demand for optical elements to link larger clusters of high-speed GPUs. But AI stocks also have become fairly volatile. After trading near $602 at the end of July, LITE stock rallied to a high of $1,143 on Oct. 9, then fell to the $800 mark within a week. LITE stock now trades at roughly $818 per share. In contrast, the iShares U.S. Telecommunications ETF (IYZ) has climbed only 14% YTD.

Story Continues

Is the Valuation Still Reasonable?

Lumentum stock trades at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 38 times, almost in line with its five-year average of roughly 37.5 times. However, its price-to-sales (P/S) ratio of 22.6 times is well above its five-year average of about 5.4 times.

This premium reflects the growth investors expect from the company as AI infrastructure spending drives demand for optical components. Analysts expect EPS to grow 143% in fiscal 2027 and another 67% in fiscal 2028. If these forecasts materialize, strong earnings growth could make the current valuation more reasonable. However, Lumentum still needs to expand production and turn its unmet demand into actual sales. Any delays or weaker-than-expected growth could put pressure on LITE stock.

Lumentum's Earnings and Growth Drivers

The latest quarterly results give investors plenty to cheer. In Q4, the company reported revenue of $1.01 billion, up 109% YOY and ahead of Wall Street's $988 million estimate. The increase was widespread throughout the company. Components revenue grew 103% YOY to $649.4 million, while Systems revenue increased 123% YOY to $356.9 million.

Profitability also improved, as gross margin climbed to 50.4% and the operating margin increased to 36.6%. On the balance sheet, free cash flow amounted to $196.2 million, while the company accumulated about $2.7 billion in cash and short-term investments by the end of the period, providing further financial flexibility.

Management anticipates the trend to persist through fiscal 2027. Lumentum is projecting an increase of more than $150 million in sales for Q1, along with gains in profitability. Revenue for the period is expected to be $1.225 billion to $1.275 billion, while adjusted EPS is projected to range between $4.05 and $4.35. CEO Michael Hurlston said that about half of the expected revenue growth will come from its components business, while the rest will come from 1.6T transceivers and faster deliveries of optical circuit switches.

What Do Analysts Expect for LITE Stock?

Analysts remain bullish after the latest earnings report. Stifel recently raised its price target from $1,100 to $1,232 and kept a "Buy" rating on shares. Meanwhile, Bernstein analyst Daniel Zhu has a "Buy" rating and a price target of $1,220 for LITE stock.

Overall, LITE stock holds a consensus "Strong Buy" rating from 25 Wall Street analysts with coverage. The mean price target of $1,169 reflects 43% potential upside from current levels, while the Street-high price target of $1,500 implies potential upside of 83% from here.

news.Title: Trading Day: AI light, Brazil flight
news.Content:
By Jamie McGeever

ORLANDO, Florida, Oct 26 (Reuters) - Stocks mostly rose on Monday, lifted by renewed optimism around AI as Anthropic filed for a US IPO and as investors awaited more 'Big Tech' earnings later this week. Weaker oil prices also support risk appetite.

The big exception, however, was Brazil, where financial assets plunged ‌following left-wing incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's shock win in Sunday's presidential election.

In my column today, I look at whether 'stagflation' pressures may be building in the US. ‌A deflating artificial intelligence bubble puts downward pressure on Wall Street and wider economic growth, but the revival of oil and energy prices is putting upward pressure on inflation. It's a tricky one for investors, and the ​Fed.

Today's Key Reads

• Brazil stocks, real tumble as Lula win ends bullish run

• Anthropic's IPO filing shows explosive growth, risks and staggering costs

• Meta eyes record $95 billion equity raise to fund AI expansion

• In China, the AI bubble has already burst

• Fed to hit pause on rate hikes, but maybe not for long

• Today's Key Market Moves STOCKS: Brazil -14%. Asia mixed, Europe and UK up around 0.8%. Wall Street higher: Nasdaq +0.8%, S&P 500 +0.7%, Dow +0.3%.SECTORS/SHARES: Seven sectors on the S&P 500 rise, four fall. Tech +1.5%, comms services -1.4%. Tesla +5%, DoorDash -6%.FX: Brazilian real -8.5%, biggest fall since devaluation in 1999. Philippine peso sinks ‌to record low near 64.00/$. US dollar index edges higher.BONDS: ⁠Brazil buys back bonds, cancels auctions. US 2-year auction is ok — foreign demand dips, domestic demand surges.COMMODITIES/METALS: Oil slips — Brent -0.8%, WTI -1.5%. Gold +0.5% back above $4,000/oz.

Today's Talking Points:

AI funding blitz

If investors were showing signs of AI fatigue in recent weeks, they're hiding it well as this week gets underway. On Monday, ⁠Anthropic filed for a US IPO, Meta announced plans for a $95 billion equity raise, and SpaceX said it has struck a $40 billion deal with Apollo Global Management for AI chip funding. The Anthropic IPO could value the company at a record-breaking $1.5 trillion or more, and Meta's capital raise would also be a record.

The eye-popping sums needed to fund the AI buildout have begun to suck some of the ​air ​out of the AI bubble, but that was shrugged off on Monday, at least temporarily — tech and AI ​stocks fueled a solid rebound on Wall Street. Competition for investor ‌capital is heating up.

Brazil

Politically, Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's surprise election victory on Sunday was truly historic: never before had a candidate won the decisive second-round vote after losing the first. It also means a record-setting fourth term for Lula, who turns 81 on Tuesday. Unsurprisingly, given the historic significance of Lula's comeback, there was a reaction across Brazilian markets.

Story Continues

Few doubt the scale of Brazil's fiscal and economic challenges, but Monday's collapse in Brazilian assets is likely to reverse, to some degree. Part of the selloff was because investors were caught so flat-footed. As late as Sunday, prediction markets were pointing to an 80% chance of a win for Senator Flavio Bolsonaro. But Lula's scope to push through an agenda that investors fear will ‌be limited, due to Bolsonaro's backing in Congress.

Central bank bonanza

This week is one of the busiest in years ​for policymaking in the world's developed economies, with half of the G10 central banks set to decide interest ​rates. Monetary authorities in New Zealand and Canada are widely expected to hike by ​25 basis points, while those in the US, euro zone and Japan are expected to keep them on hold but signal possible increases in ‌December.

The common enemy is inflation, which is already too sticky in many ​countries. Oil and global energy prices remain elevated ​as war continues to choke Middle East supply routes, and the worry for policymakers is this bleeds into core inflation and becomes embedded in inflation expectations. But if the AI bubble deflates, growth, consumer confidence and investor sentiment could deflate too, putting policymakers in an even tighter bind.

What could move markets tomorrow?

• Japan services producer price inflation (September)

• ​South Korea GDP (Q3, advance)

• US Treasury sells $70 billion of 5-year notes ‌at auction

• US durable goods (September)

• Corporate earnings, including Visa, Coca-Cola, Boeing, Seagate Technology, HSBC, Novartis

news.Title: Why Google might avoid an earnings 'reckoning' this week
news.Content:
Google's ( GOOG ) investors have a few things in their favor coming into earnings day this week that Meta ( META ) investors weren't afforded when the tech giant reported a few negative surprises .

"Google has already done some of its fundraising and indicated a 'significant' increase in capex next year when it reported Q2, so that particular reckoning may be behind it," D.A. Davidson analyst Gil Luria wrote in a note on Monday. "It is worth noting that Mr. Brin and Mr. Page moved out of California before the 1/1/26 cutoff and may be able to avoid having to sell their shares. Which means that investors will be able to focus on the Anthropic-driven growth in Google Cloud."

Meta surprised investors last week on several fronts.

The company posted negative free cash flow for the first time since 2012 amid aggressive AI spending. It signaled more aggressive spending in coming quarters.

To fund that spending, it further surprised investors by establishing a new class of nonvoting Class C common stock, which effectively serves as a 2-for-1 stock split.

Under the scheme — in part designed to keep founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg working in California as the 5% billionaire's tax looms — existing shareholders will receive one new nonvoting Class C share for every Class A or Class B share they hold. Trading is slated to begin in January 2027.

Issuing nonvoting stock allows Zuckerberg to raise external capital for Meta's AI build-out without diluting his personal voting control over the tech giant.

Meta shares have come under pressure on fears Zuckerberg may have to sell shares to pay for his Prop 40 tax bill.

But as Luria pointed out, Google investors need not worry on this front.

Co-founder Larry Page bought two Miami estates for a combined $173.4 million, the Wall Street Journal reported earlier this year. His co-founder, Sergey Brin, moved to the Nevada side of Lake Tahoe and also bought a home in Miami this year, Fortune reported.

"We expect the company to discuss its plans to regain primacy in AI, where it is now a 2nd or 3rd place in each of the markets — 2nd in chat to ChatGPT, 3rd in enterprise to Anthropic and OpenAI, and now even trailing Meta's Muse in the personal AI assistant market," Luria wrote about Google's upcoming earnings report.

news.Title: Not AMD. Not Marvell. Here's Which Company Nvidia Needs to Be Worried About.
news.Content:
Nvidia holds the title for the largest market share in the artificial intelligence (AI) computing unit market. Its GPUs have become synonymous with AI computing power, but it's not without competition.

One of the more obvious picks is Advanced Micro Devices , as it also makes GPUs. However, AMD's data center division is far smaller than Nvidia's and also grew at a slower rate during its most recent quarters.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

However, GPUs aren't the only way AI computing is done. While GPUs are incredibly flexible and can do a lot of tasks, they aren't optimized for any one workload. There are many tasks that need to be done on a repetitive basis in the AI world, and a specialized computing unit can thrive in these tasks.

This is where I see the biggest threat to Nvidia's business, and there are two key players in this industry.

Custom AI chips are expected to become more popular in the future

The two primary custom AI chip firms are Marvell and Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO). Marvell's primary clients are Microsoft and Amazon , while Broadcom has partnered with Alphabet , Meta Platforms , Anthropic, and OpenAI. Marvell and Broadcom are very similar to AMD and Nvidia. While Marvell has the business and is competing, it doesn't have the size. Marvell's AI data center revenue totaled $2.1 billion in Q2.

Broadcom's AI semiconductor revenue reached $16.7 billion. Broadcom is the company to beat in this industry, and I think it's one that Nvidia actually needs to worry about.

The crown jewel of Broadcom's custom AI chip empire is Google's Tensor Processing Unit (TPU), a device that Broadcom and Alphabet have collaborated on for a long time. These units have gone through several generations and are even starting to be sold on the market by Alphabet because there's such high demand for them. Broadcom's other clients will look to recreate these units optimized for their own workloads, and Broadcom will benefit significantly from growth in this area.

This year, they estimate their AI segment revenue will be around $58 billion. However, that figure is expected to reach $115 billion in 2027 and $230 billion in 2028. For reference, Nvidia expects its 2027 revenue growth to be about 70% so that Broadcom will be growing at a slower pace. This points to Broadcom taking market share from Nvidia as the build-out grows. Still, it will never fully replace Nvidia, as GPUs are useful in many situations that custom AI chips aren't.

Story Continues

This leaves a major market open for both stocks, although Broadcom may be in a better position to capture more business. However, its stock isn't really pricing in any growth for 2027.

Broadcom's stock isn't expensive

Broadcom currently trades at 43 times trailing earnings, which isn't super cheap. However, it doesn't price in the massive growth it's expected to undergo next year.

AVGO PE Ratio data by YCharts

With the shares trading at 17 times next year's earnings estimates, it shows the market expects huge growth. If Broadcom rose to 35 times earnings by the end of next fiscal year, it would indicate that the stock has the potential to double.

That's a solid return in a short time frame, but remember, Broadcom also said it would double its revenue base again in 2028. That means there are multiple years of strong returns ahead for Broadcom. With it gaining new clients in the AI sector, there's a lot of opportunity for Broadcom to firmly establish itself alongside Nvidia as a major leader in the AI computing space . SIMO Estimate Trend

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Earnings Surprise History

The leading NAND flash controller designer has a modest trailing four-quarter earnings surprise history, having exceeded expectations on three occasions. It delivered a four-quarter earnings surprise of 13.96%, on average. In the last reported quarter, the company delivered an earnings surprise of 14.08%.

Factors Shaping Upcoming Results

During the quarter, Silicon Motion unveiled its MonTitan SSD Reference Design Kit, targeting AI infrastructure with high-performance, scalable storage solutions. The kit helps accelerate SSD development, enabling faster data processing, improved efficiency and optimized storage performance for demanding AI workloads, data centers and next-generation computing systems.

The company is expected to benefit from growing demand for enterprise storage solutions, AI infrastructure and automotive applications in the third quarter of 2026. Management expects revenues to increase 15-20% sequentially, supported primarily by its Ferri automotive storage products, enterprise boot drive solutions and MonTitan enterprise SSD controllers. The ongoing commercial ramp of MonTitan, coupled with healthy customer order patterns across storage solutions, is expected to support the company's near-term performance.

SIMO's embedded storage business is another potential growth driver. The company continues to gain market share in eMMC and UFS controllers as NAND suppliers focus more resources on higher-priority memory products. However, rising NAND and DRAM prices remain a potential headwind. Higher component costs are making smartphones and PCs less affordable, particularly in lower-priced segments

Story Continues

Price Performance

Over the past year, SIMO has surged 81.9% compared with the industry's growth of 97.6%. It has underperformed peers like Marvell Technology, Inc. MRVL and Western Digital Corporation WDC over this period. While Marvell has gained 157.5%, WDC has jumped 171.3%.

Key Valuation Metric

From a valuation standpoint, Silicon Motion appears to be trading at a premium relative to the industry and above its mean. Going by the price/earnings ratio, the company's shares currently trade at 12.17 forward earnings, higher than 9.6 for the industry but lower than the stock's mean of 22.81.

Investment Considerations

SIMO's expanding exposure to enterprise storage, automotive applications and AI infrastructure strengthens its long-term growth opportunity. The company's controller technology, established relationships with NAND manufacturers, and growing presence in higher-value storage solutions could help it capture demand as computing workloads become more storage-intensive. The increasing contribution of MonTitan and enterprise boot drive products also offers an opportunity to reduce dependence on consumer-oriented markets over time.

Profitability is another factor worth monitoring. Management expects the third quarter to benefit from a more favorable product mix, particularly the rising contribution of MonTitan and PCIe Gen5 controllers.

However, SIMO is exposed to volatility in the consumer market. Weak smartphone and PC demand, elevated memory prices, intense competition and uncertainty surrounding component availability could limit growth in established product categories.

End Note

Expanding enterprise storage operations, market-share gains in embedded controllers and increasing demand for automotive and AI-related storage solutions are major tailwinds as SIMO is set to release third-quarter results. Nevertheless, higher memory costs, weakness in consumer markets and the pace of enterprise product adoption remain key variables. SIMO's diversification strategy boosts prospects for the long run, but in the near term, the company demonstrates a balanced outlook. Long-term investors should hold on to the stock, but new investors should wait for a better entry point.

news.Title: Chip Stocks to Buy After Their Worst Day Since June
news.Content:
Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX), which sells chipmaking equipment, reported record revenue on Oct. 21. It also said limited clean-room space and shortages of some parts would stop chipmakers and equipment companies from fully meeting demand into 2027.

The PHLX Semiconductor Index dropped 6.7% on Oct. 22, its worst day since June 23. Lam lost 12%, Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) 6%, Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) 8%, and Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) 9%.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

But Lam was describing more demand than the industry can meet, not less. And all three chipmakers' own outlooks still point up. I think the sell-off makes all three worth buying.

Image source: Getty Images.

Lam's issue is supply, not demand

Lam's revenue rose 22% from the June quarter to $8.22 billion, up 54% year over year. And management still forecast around $8.6 billion in the December quarter.

"[T]his revenue guide would have been a bit higher if not for some near-term supply chain constraints," CFO Doug Bettinger said on the earnings call.

Lam also expects industry spending on chipmaking equipment to pass $200 billion in 2027, up from the mid-$150 billion range this year. Asked what that number would be without the constraints, Bettinger said it "would be higher."

Micron: short on clean rooms, not customers

On Sept. 30, memory maker Micron said industry supply of DRAM and NAND (the two main kinds of memory chips) should stay constrained in 2027 and 2028.

"We expect memory and storage supply-demand conditions to be much tighter in calendar 2027 and 2028 than they were in 2026," CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said in prepared remarks for that day's call.

Showing what tight supply has done for Micron, its revenue rose 31% sequentially to $54.2 billion in the fiscal fourth quarter of 2026 (which ended Sept. 3), as DRAM prices climbed by a high-teens percentage and NAND prices by about 30%. Management expects another record in the fiscal first quarter of 2027, at roughly $61.5 billion, and to grow in every quarter of fiscal 2027. But the stock is off 29% from its June 25 record close, at about $856 as I write, or about 5 times earnings for fiscal 2027 on analysts' consensus. That price suggests investors expect memory profits to fall soon. Micron is predicting the opposite.

Story Continues

AMD: the upside hinges on supply

AMD is supply-limited, too. In Taipei on Oct. 6, CEO Lisa Su said it plans to substantially increase supply in 2027 and needs more advanced wafer capacity.

On AMD's August earnings call, Su said she saw nothing that gave her pause about meeting its targets. That suggests the limits Lam flagged could matter more for how far AMD beats its plan than for the plan itself. Management guided for around $13 billion in third-quarter revenue, up about 41% year over year, and expects data center sales, led by its artificial intelligence (AI) chips, to more than double next year.

AMD stock, at about $508, is 22% under its Oct. 6 record close. Shares cost around 32 times earnings, based on analysts' consensus for 2027, so the price already counts on that data center doubling.

Marvell: a higher profit target

At its Oct. 6 investor day, Marvell targeted $70 billion to $90 billion of revenue for fiscal 2031 (ending early 2031) and a non-GAAP (adjusted) operating margin of 44% to 46%. Management said the midpoint of those targets implies adjusted earnings of more than $30 a share. Marvell brought in $8.2 billion in fiscal 2026.

Its revenue growth is already picking up, from 28% year over year in the fiscal first quarter of 2027 to 37% in the fiscal second quarter (which ended Aug. 1), and management expects about $3.15 billion in fiscal third-quarter revenue, roughly 52% above the year-ago quarter.

But at about $223, shares are 22% under their Oct. 6 close. They cost about 31 times earnings, based on analysts' consensus for fiscal 2028, but only about 7 times the earnings Marvell is targeting for fiscal 2031. Of course, that target's over four years off, and Marvell depends on outside manufacturers for its chips -- the sort of chipmakers Lam says can't fully meet demand.

Is the sell-off a buying opportunity?

None of these companies has cut its outlook, and all three stocks just got cheaper.

Micron's the one I'd buy first. Tight supply is already boosting its prices, and the stock's arguably priced for a downturn its own outlook doesn't show.

AMD and Marvell are pricier growth stocks that need their plans to hold up to justify over 30 times expected earnings. I think both are worth considering here, ideally a bit at a time. After all, a slowdown in AI spending might still hit all three stocks hard.

news.Title: Prediction: 2 Stocks That Will Be Worth More Than AMD 5 Years From Now
news.Content:
AMD (NASDAQ: AMD) has become a major winner in the artificial intelligence (AI) boom. But Cerebras Systems (NASDAQ: CBRS) and Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL) are taking different approaches to AI that could make them far more valuable than AMD over the next five years.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Cerebras is the more unconventional of the two, and the best place to start.

Cerebras is the AI chip challenger built for speed

For years, the AI chip race has been about building more powerful processors and connecting them to more complex systems. Cerebras is taking a different route: building an enormous chip designed specifically to make AI compute faster and less complicated.

That edge is becoming increasingly important as AI moves beyond chatbots toward autonomous agents and coding assistants. These applications don't just need compute power; they need answers quickly. In fact, Cerebras has built its whole platform around that need.

Its second-quarter 2026 results showed core revenue more than doubling year over year, while cloud revenue nearly quadrupled. On top of that, Cerebras reported $25.4 billion in remaining performance obligations (RPO), strengthening visibility into future revenue.

Management also expects core revenue to more than triple in 2027, after guiding for between $880 million and $890 million this year.

While the company hasn't offered any projections through 2031, if history repeats and Cerebras keeps roughly doubling its revenue each year, it could reach about $28 billion by 2031, compared with Marvell's target of $70 billion to $90 billion.

Plus, the company's partnerships could be just as important as its chips. Cerebras has worked with OpenAI on fast inference and partnered with AMD to combine speed with higher throughput.

It also expanded its relationship with Amazon 's AWS, potentially opening the door to wider enterprise adoption through Amazon Bedrock. If these collaborations continue, Cerebras could see stronger demand for its technology without needing to build an entire software and distribution system from scratch.

That said, the company still faces several risks. Customer concentration and competition from established chipmakers are both risks to the bull case, as is potential dilution as the company funds its expansion.

Story Continues

For Cerebras to catch up to AMD, it would need to establish a large, defensible AI compute business and convert its technological edge into durable profits.

But speed isn't the only way to approach the AI boom. Another company is building the infrastructure that keeps data centers running.

A pick-and-shovel supplier in the AI boom

Marvell is pursuing another strategy to win a larger share of AI compute: supplying custom chips and high-speed connections that power AI data centers.

As cloud companies build out their AI infrastructure, they aren't simply buying more off-the-shelf processors. Instead, they're designing more specialized chips to handle their own workloads, improve efficiency, and reduce dependence on any single chip supplier.

Marvell is positioned for this shift through its exposure to custom compute and networking hardware.

The company's relationships with major cloud providers matter to the investment case. For example, Alphabet , Microsoft , and Meta Platforms are among the hyperscalers investing heavily in AI infrastructure. That creates opportunities for Marvell to supply the chips and connectivity that tie these systems together.

Optical networking is also becoming an important growth driver at Marvell. As AI clusters expand, moving data between chips and servers becomes more challenging.

That means Marvell's expertise in optical technology and data center connectivity gives it exposure to this growing bottleneck in data center infrastructure.

The main risk now is that Marvell's growth targets depend on a small group of large customers. Meanwhile, custom chip programs can be delayed, customers can switch suppliers, and competition from other chipmakers could put pressure on margins.

But if Marvell scales to anywhere near management's long-term ambitions, it could become more valuable than AMD within five years. In fact, the company's goal is to 10x its revenue by fiscal 2031, from just $8.2 billion in fiscal 2026 to $70 billion-$90 billion.

Plus, by participating in several layers of the AI build-out, Marvell could very well achieve this ambitious target.

Of course, the market already has a view on how much growth to expect.

Can these two stocks outgrow AMD over the next five years?

AMD's market cap is roughly $829 billion, compared with $195 billion for Marvell and $26 billion for Cerebras. That means both have a lot of ground to make up.

Marvell looks like the best bet as it already has an established business and relationships with the biggest cloud companies worldwide.

Cerebras is the high-risk, high-reward pick, with faster growth but also customer concentration, dilution, and a high valuation.

Either could eventually surpass AMD based on their ambitions, but Cerebras could face a bumpier ride.

news.Title: Marvell’s Road to $90B: The 3 Moves Behind the Boldest Target in AI Chips
news.Content:
Investors don't have to bet on Nvidia (NVDA) alone to benefit from AI chip spending. Marvell Technology (MRVL) ranks among the top global chipmakers, thanks to its role in custom AI chips and data center connectivity. As companies develop more of their own processors due to the AI boom, Marvell could benefit from designing those chips and connecting the systems around them. This opportunity has led management to raise its fiscal 2028 revenue target to $20 billion. But can earnings grow fast enough to justify the stock's valuation?

Custom AI Chips Are Just One Part of Marvell's Growth Story

In my view, Marvell's biggest advantage is that its revenue streams are not just dependent on processors. The company raised its fiscal 2031 revenue target to $70 billion to $90 billion at its Oct. 6 investor day. It also expects custom chip revenue to exceed $12 billion in fiscal 2029. But I believe the broader opportunity is just as important. Marvell also sees opportunities in XPU-attached products, which add networking, memory, and other functions to AI processors. These products could give Marvell another source of growth beyond designing complete custom chips. CEO Matt Murphy's comments on the company's broader connectivity portfolio further support this thesis.

Dear SoFi Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendar for October 27

Our exclusive Barchart Brief newsletter is your FREE midday guide to what's moving stocks, sectors, and investor sentiment - delivered right when you need the info most. Subscribe today!

About Marvell Stock

Marvell Technology is a semiconductor company that provides data infrastructure solutions used in data centers, networking systems, and communication equipment worldwide. The company designs advanced chips that move, process, and store data efficiently. It offers a portfolio of Ethernet solutions, networking controllers, processors, storage controllers, optical and interconnect solutions, and custom chips. Marvell focuses on technologies that improve high-speed data transfer, connectivity, and AI infrastructure performance. Founded in 1995, the company is headquartered in Wilmington, Delaware.

Over the last 12 months, Marvell has significantly outperformed the semiconductor sector, with the stock climbing roughly 202%. This was well above the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX), which gained about 79% during the same period. The rally was driven by growing demand for AI data-center infrastructure, including custom AI chips and high-speed networking solutions. Moreover, Marvell's fiscal 2026 revenue rose 42% to a record $8.2 billion, while data-center revenue jumped 46% to $6.1 billion.

Story Continues

Marvell's forward P/E of 53.98x is steep, sitting about 42% above its five-year average of 38.05x. Its forward price-to-sales ratio of 16.55x is also 61% above its historical average of 10.25x. So the stock is more expensive than usual, even as investors bet on its AI opportunity. The earnings outlook helps explain the premium. Analysts expect EPS to grow 48.6% in fiscal 2027 and 72.89% in fiscal 2028. If Marvell delivers that growth, its earnings could begin to justify the valuation.

Expensive, but Earnings Could Catch Up

Marvell Technology reported its second-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings on August 27. For Q2 fiscal 2027, data-centre revenue increased 46% YOY to $2.17 billion, representing 79% of total revenue. The data-center segment is expected to remain the key growth driver, with Marvell having expanded commercial agreements with Tier 1 hyperscalers for multiple custom products. The non-GAAP earnings per share came in at $0.94, beating the Wall Street estimates of $0.93. At the same time, Marvell reported an operating cash flow of $605.5 million. This implies an annualized OCF potential of $2.42 billion.

Since the valuation might be a potential deterrent for investors, it's important to also talk about the growth trajectory. Marvell guided for 45% revenue growth in fiscal 2027 to $12 billion. Further, the company expects 50% revenue growth in fiscal 2028 to $18 billion. Even beyond fiscal 2028, the outlook remains positive. For example, Marvell is positioned for $10 billion to $11 billion in custom-silicon business for fiscal 2029. The company has a custom-silicon partnership with Alphabet's (GOOG) Google, which should have a meaningful impact on revenue.

What Do Analysts Expect for MRVL Stock?

The analyst outlook for Marvell Technology is significantly positive. Based on 39 analysts with coverage, MRVL stock has a consensus "Strong Buy" rating on Wall Street. While 30 analysts have a "Strong Buy" rating for the stock, three have a "Moderate Buy," and six have a "Hold" rating.

The mean price target of $337.05 represents potential upside of 38% from current levels. Meanwhile, the most bullish price target of $450 suggests that MRVL stock could climb as much as 84% from here.

news.Title: 聯發科TPU進度遭質疑！ 花旗法說前送暖：目標上看6800元
news.Content:
面對市場對聯發科TPU發展的疑慮，花旗證券於法說前夕出面力挺，看好受惠於AI ASIC貢獻與消費性產品漲價，第四季營收將迎來約30%的強勁季增，重申買進評等並維持目標價6,800元。

法說前夕送暖力挺

IC設計龍頭廠聯發科（2454）預計於10月30日召開線上法人說明會，公佈第三季財務報告與第四季業績展望。儘管近期市場對於聯發科的張量處理器（TPU）開發與新專案進展存有疑慮，但花旗證券在最新研究報告中發布正面看法，認為營運長線成長趨勢依舊明確，並給予正面評價。

AI ASIC與消費產品雙引擎

花旗分析指出，聯發科的v8專案正按計畫順利推進，今年超過20億美元的營收貢獻，將成為帶動第四季營收季增長的核心催化劑。結合消費性產品的價格調漲與產品組合改善，預期第四季營收可獲得約30%的季增表現，且在營運槓桿效益帶動下，營業利益率亦具備上行空間。

先進封裝與技術佈局延伸

針對市場對EMIB-T技術面臨良率挑戰與週期較長所引發的v9生產風險疑慮，花旗表示此狀況已在預料之中。然而，受惠於v8專案的長期成長動能，加上SerDes升級與N2製程開發帶動平均售價提升，花旗維持2028年AI ASIC營收貢獻達400億美元的預測。技術進展方面，聯發科除已量產的224G SerDes外，336G與448G SerDes也在積極開發中。此外，針對瞄準2029年量產的TPU v10，聯發科有很大機會採用CoWOS或CoPoS封裝技術，相關訂單能見度已延伸至2029年之後。

生態系合作與財務預估上調

花旗強調，聯發科憑藉先進製程設計能力、SerDes開發技術、供應鏈管理能力及靈活的商業模式，有極大機會進一步滲透至新的雲端服務供應商專案中。同時，聯發科亦為NVLink Fusion生態系中，少數具備前端設計與全流程AI ASIC服務能力的重要玩家，將為2028年之後帶來長遠發展契機。基於營運槓桿與AI ASIC的爆發性成長，花旗將聯發科2026年、2027年及2028年的獲利預估分別調升9%、25%與9%，並重申「買進」評等目標價6,800元。

news.Title: 5 big analyst AI moves: ’Uniquely catalyst-rich’ months ahead for SpaceX
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Here are the biggest analyst moves in the area of artificial intelligence (AI) for this week.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

Loop Capital downgrades Apple after supply chain checks reveal no iPhone recovery plan

Brokerage firm Loop Capital this week downgraded Apple to Hold from Buy and cut its price target to $330 from $370, after supply chain checks revealed Apple has no plans to recover the 13 million iPhone shipments cut in the second half of 2026.

Analyst Ananda Baruah said Apple previously reduced September- and December-quarter iPhone shipments by 10%, with Loop having initially believed those units could be made up through 2027 as the reductions were supply-related rather than demand-driven.

"This no longer appears to be the case," Baruah wrote.

Loop lowered its December-quarter iPhone unit forecast to 79 million from the Street's 85 million, cutting its average selling price (ASP) estimate to $1,123 from $1,239. For calendar 2027, it raised its unit forecast to 260 million but cut ASP to $1,096 from $1,235, lowering iPhone revenue to $285 billion from $315 billion and trimming EPS to $9.76 from $10.11.

The broker also flagged potential gross margin risk as memory costs keep rising, lowering its normalized EPS estimate to $11 from $12 and applying Apple's median P/E of 30 times to arrive at the new target.

"We continue to like AAPL's longer-term share gain and Services story… but believe the stock also requires a fundamental catalyst reset after its recent stock appreciation," Baruah said.

JPMorgan upgrades Intel as pullback from peak makes risk-reward more balanced

JPMorgan has upgraded Intel to Neutral from Underweight, saying the risk/reward is now much more balanced as the stock approaches the bank's $85 price target after pulling back roughly 40% from its June peak, compared with a 20-25% decline for the broader chip group.

Analyst Harlan Sur noted that since JPMorgan downgraded the stock in November 2022, Intel's server x86 CPU revenue share has fallen from 77% to 53% and its PC CPU share from 81% to 68%, with a few more quarters of share losses expected, particularly in server CPUs.

In foundry, Intel appears to be making strong inroads on yields and new customer engagements, though it generated barely $1 billion in annualized external foundry revenue in the first half of 2026, compared with $150 billion for TSMC.

Sur said that since Lip Bu Tan became CEO, execution has improved in Intel's core client and data center compute markets and in next-generation manufacturing. "Despite near-term concerns on AI infrastructure spending sustainability, we believe increasing agentic AI workloads (CPU intensive) and a very tight supply chain for leading edge silicon should drive continued positive EPS revisions in the upcoming earnings season and through CY27," he wrote.

Story Continues

JPMorgan's 2028 EPS estimates sit about 15% above consensus.

"Risk/reward is more balanced at current levels and we move to a Neutral rating," Sur said.

Citi opens positive Catalyst Watch on SpaceX, sees coming months as "uniquely catalyst-rich"

Earlier in the week, Citi opened a positive 90-day Catalyst Watch on SpaceX, arguing the coming months will be "uniquely catalyst rich," after the company reported revenue that more than doubled in the third quarter and posted net income of $4.4 billion, its first profitable quarter as a public company.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Growth was driven largely by SpaceX's AI segment, with space and connectivity businesses also expanding. CEO Elon Musk also offered some of his most detailed comments yet on a potential merger with Tesla, saying the move would be "a good idea" and confirming for the first time that special committees had been formed to discuss a potential union.

Musk said he expects annual recurring revenue (ARR) to reach between $500 billion and $1 trillion by end-2027, driven by surging demand for data-center space amid the AI boom.

Citi, which rates the stock Buy, pointed to six factors behind its positive catalyst watch: SpaceX's "track record of beats/raises" expected to continue into the fourth quarter; Flight 15 as "a monumental space-industry catalyst that sets the stage for rapid reusability on a scale never before demonstrated in launch"; dollar-per-watt economics "trending significantly above consensus expectations"; an accelerated Grok model release cadence; the possibility of more detail on SpaceX's power-generation solutions before year-end; and further clarity on its "evolving mobile strategy."

"We've described Buy-rated SPCX as being in the midst of a catalyst-rich 2-3 year arc, and we see the next 2-3 months in particular as uniquely catalyst rich even within that timeline that supports our positive investment thesis," Citi analysts said.

Buy Lam Research on pullback, Mizuho says

Mizuho has reiterated its Outperform rating on Lam Research and recommended buying the stock after a significant pullback following quarterly results, trimming its price target to $360 from $365.

Analyst Vijay Rakesh highlighted that Lam expects wafer fab equipment (WFE) spending to grow more than 29% in 2027 to over $200 billion, after rising about 42% to roughly $155 billion this year. "We are buyers on the pullback, as new greenfield fabs, NAND/HBM/Terafab position for upside," he wrote, also flagging Tesla's comments pointing to "10s of $B WFE" from Terafab in early 2028 and $100 billion long-term.

Mizuho highlighted the emergence of SLC NAND as a major tailwind, with each 1 percentage point mix shift requiring 2% more NAND wafer capacity — a market where Lam holds about 90% share. NAND revenue rose 38% in the September quarter and foundry grew 28%. The broker estimates Lam's revenue will grow 37% next year, ahead of 30% consensus, and believes Lam sees 10 new tier 1 fabs coming online in 2027.

"We see LRCX well positioned with: 1) wide competitive moats, 2) secular technology trends with HPC/AI/ML, HBM/CoWoS/TSV, GAA/BPD, and 3) rising capital intensity at the leading edge," Rakesh said.

Lam reported September-quarter revenue of $8.22 billion and EPS of $2.20, broadly in line with consensus, with gross margin rising 40 basis points sequentially to 52.4%. December-quarter guidance of $8.6 billion in revenue and EPS of $2.33 came in slightly above expectations.

AI bubble exists but will not burst yet: Yardeni

This week, Financial research firm Yardeni Research introduced an AI Bubble Meter, built using Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1, which it says confirms a bubble exists in AI-related stocks but shows it is not yet close to bursting.

The tool has two dials. The Conditions dial measures whether a bubble exists by drawing on the setups that preceded the 1999-2000 tech bust and the 2006-2007 housing bust, and currently reads 83 out of 100. The Triggers dial tracks whether the forces that ended past booms — a credit boom and a sustained rise in the cost of capital — are underway, and reads just 34.

"The meter says there's a bubble, but it's not about to burst," Yardeni wrote.

One trigger has kicked in, with the two-year Treasury yield up 115 basis points from its December low, but credit is not stretched outside AI-related areas of the economy. "The preconditions of a bubble are in place and have been for a while, but the forces that ended past booms are only partially present," the firm said.

Yardeni noted that since 1965, quarters with high Conditions and low Triggers readings were followed by an S&P 500 bear market within two years only 9% of the time, with a median inflation-adjusted gain of 18.3% over that period. When both dials read high, the odds of a bear market rose to 42% with a median loss of 12.5%.

"But the Triggers dial is the one to watch: If it starts rising toward High, so do the risks," Yardeni said, flagging the two-year yield and signs of idle capacity in hyperscalers' third-quarter results as key things to monitor.
