news.Title: Prediction: Sandisk Stock Will Soar After Oct. 29. Here Are 379 Billion Reasons Why
news.Content:
Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) stock has fallen from grace in recent months after delivering a stunning performance in the first half of 2026.

Shares of the flash storage specialist have pulled back 32% since the beginning of July. For comparison, Sandisk stock rose by a stunning 858% in the first half of 2026. The recent slide in Sandisk stock has nothing to do with the company's financial performance. Investors have pressed the panic button and are booking profits in Sandisk amid concerns about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure build-out .

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

However, a closer look at the developments in the NAND flash industry suggests that the fears about a slowdown in Sandisk's growth are overblown. In fact, I won't be surprised to see the company deliver stronger-than-expected fiscal 2027 first-quarter results on Oct. 29.

Let's check the reasons why Sandisk stock could take off following its upcoming quarterly report.

Image source: Getty Images.

Sandisk's growth and potential don't justify its slide

The incredible demand for NAND flash storage in AI data centers has been Sandisk's biggest growth driver. The resulting supply shortage has led to a massive increase in NAND flash prices, which explains the red-hot growth in Sandisk's revenue and earnings.

The company expects fiscal Q1 revenue of $10.3-$10.8 billion, along with non-GAAP earnings of $45.00 per share. The guidance implies a year-over-year increase of 357% in revenue at the midpoint, along with a 37x jump in non-GAAP earnings per share. Market research firm TrendForce expects NAND flash prices to surge by 235% in 2026, which explains why Sandisk is anticipating such phenomenal growth in fiscal Q1.

Even better, analysts expect Sandisk to sustain its red-hot growth in the current quarter as well. Consensus estimates on Yahoo! Finance predict a 4x year-over-year increase in Sandisk's revenue in the current quarter to $12.2 billion. Meanwhile, earnings per share could increase by 8x to $52.94. So, the recent slide in Sandisk's stock price isn't justified when we consider that the strong NAND flash demand and price environment will continue to remain a tailwind for the company.

Moreover, the NAND flash market is poised for further growth in 2027. TrendForce expects NAND flash industry revenue to reach $379 billion in 2027, up 40% from this year. Of course, the market's growth rate is expected to slow substantially next year compared with 2026's estimated 280%, but that's still a healthy number.

Story Continues

Importantly, Sandisk can make the most of this huge opportunity given that it controls 11% of the NAND flash market, according to Counterpoint Research. A similar share of this market at the end of 2027 could send Sandisk's revenue in calendar 2027 to almost $42 billion, double the revenue it has generated over the past twelve months.

So, Sandisk seems poised to grow at a robust pace over the next year and a half, given the incredible $379 billion addressable opportunity it is sitting on. Throw in the fact that the NAND flash industry will remain undersupplied in 2027 and 2028, according to Citi , and Sandisk should also be able to clock healthy earnings growth.

This probably explains why there has been a slight uptick in Sandisk's earnings per share expectations for the current and the next fiscal year.

SNDK EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts

A stronger-than-expected outlook can supercharge the stock

One of the reasons why this AI stock has been under pressure lately is because of concerns that NAND flash supply growth will overtake demand next year. This could erase the pricing advantage that Sandisk has been enjoying.

However, the points discussed above suggest otherwise. Additionally, robust NAND flash demand from AI servers could lead to a sequential increase of 15%-20% in NAND flash contract prices in the current quarter, according to TrendForce. This is why I think Sandisk's guidance for the ongoing quarter may exceed expectations, giving the stock a much-needed boost.

Another reason why Sandisk seems like a no-brainer buy right now is that it trades at an extremely cheap 8 times forward earnings. The S&P 500 index, for comparison, has a forward earnings multiple of 19. Sandisk should ideally trade at a significant premium given its exponential growth rate. So, it makes sense for savvy investors to buy this growth stock before Oct. 29 as strong results and a sunny guidance could set it up for a strong finish to the year.

news.Title: Vicor Corporation Shares Gain 4.5% on Strong Q3 Earnings Growth
news.Content:
Vicor Corporation VICR shares have gained 4.5% since it reported third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 20. The uptick can be attributed to strong AI-driven demand and rising recurring royalty revenues, which lifted sales, margins and profitability.

The company reported third-quarter 2026 earnings of $1.33 per share, missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 4.32%. The figure increased 111.1% year over year.

Revenues surged 78.5% year over year to $197.11 million and surpassed the consensus estimate by 5.4%. Strong Advanced Products sales and higher royalty income supported growth. The company's order backlog increased 166% year over year to $406 million, reflecting robust demand.

VICR's Advanced Products Revenues Accelerate

Advanced Products revenues, including royalties, increased 47.5% sequentially to $138.9 million. The business accounted for 70.4% of total revenues, up from 65.7% in the preceding quarter.

Vicor Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Vicor Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Vicor Corporation Quote

Brick Products revenues increased 18.4% sequentially to $58.3 million and represented 29.6% of total revenues.

Shipments to stocking distributors increased 24.8% sequentially and 16.2% year over year. Exports accounted for approximately 36.1% of revenues, down from 46% in the second quarter of 2026.

Vicor Benefits From Expanding Royalty Income

Product revenues totaled $130.5 million, up 47.1% year over year. Royalty revenues surged 206.6% year over year to $66.6 million from $21.7 million. Sequentially, royalty revenues increased 119.1%, supported by licensing agreements.

The company granted its first vertical power delivery (VPD) license to a leading artificial intelligence (AI) original equipment manufacturer at Stage 2-unit royalty rates. Management noted that part of the quarterly royalty contribution reflected initial payments, while the underlying licensing arrangements provide recurring income.

Vicor also received inquiries from hyperscalers regarding broader licensing agreements. Management expects royalty income to grow as additional customers adopt its intellectual property, although the timing of payments and new agreements could create quarterly fluctuations.

VICR's Backlog Reflects Strong Market Demand

The book-to-bill ratio remained above 1, while backlog increased 7% sequentially to $380 million. Management highlighted approximately $100 million in bookings during the first two weeks of the fourth quarter, including a substantial order for second-generation VPD modules.

Demand remained strong across AI computing, automatic test equipment (ATE), industrial, aerospace and defense markets. The company's ATE business, which serves semiconductor and memory testing applications, now generates more than $100 million in annual revenues.

Management highlighted growing customer interest in second-generation VPD technology following demonstrations at Open Compute. The technology aims to address increasing power density and efficiency requirements for advanced AI processors.

Story Continues

Vicor's Margins Expand Despite Rising Expenses

Gross profit increased sequentially to $134.7 million from $83.1 million. Gross margin expanded 1,030 basis points to 68.3%, benefiting from higher royalty revenues, improved product mix, manufacturing efficiencies and increased volumes.

Operating expenses increased 29.6% sequentially to $62.5 million. Legal expenses, a substantial portion of which are linked to royalty revenues, increased approximately $11.1 million to $16.1 million. Management expects legal expenses to average approximately 20% of royalty revenues in the near term.

Operating income surged 245.1% year over year to $72.1 million from $20.9 million in the year-ago quarter.

VICR Strengthens Cash Position and Expands Capacity

As of Sept. 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents totaled $513.1 million compared with $453.6 million in the previous quarter.

Operating activities generated $69.7 million in cash compared with $34 million in the second quarter.

Vicor acquired two additional manufacturing sites within 30 miles of its existing Andover facility. The planned Fab-2 and Fab-3 facilities could increase manufacturing capacity nearly fivefold relative to Fab-1.

Management expects initial equipment deployment at Fab-2 in the second quarter of 2027. The expansion will initially target capacity-constrained manufacturing processes. The company expects to fund its expansion plans without raising additional capital.

Vicor Expects Further Product Revenue Growth

Vicor expects fourth-quarter 2026 product revenues to increase approximately 10% sequentially. The outlook assumes another double-digit sequential increase in Advanced Products hardware revenues.

Management also expects at least $43 million in fourth-quarter royalty revenues, assuming no additional licensing agreements. Existing arrangements could generate incremental royalties beyond this baseline.

The company anticipates further margin expansion as revenues increase and manufacturing utilization improves. However, near-term capacity constraints at Fab-1 remain a consideration as Vicor works to expand production capabilities and meet growing customer demand.

Zacks Rank & Upcoming Earnings to Watch

Vicor currently sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy).

Alkami Technology, ASE Technology and Entegris are expected to report their quarterly results on Oct. 28, Oct. 29 and Oct. 29, respectively. While Shares of ASE Technology and Entegris have surged 163.5% and 75.3%, respectively, Alkami Technology shares have plunged 34.5% in the year-to-date period.

news.Title: Can Semiconductor Systems Drive AMAT's Next Growth Phase?
news.Content:
Applied Materials AMAT is gaining from rising demand for advanced chips used in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, especially in its Semiconductor Systems business. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, Semiconductor Systems generated revenues of $7.04 billion, up approximately 27% year over year.

Growing investment in leading-edge foundry-logic, dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) and advanced packaging is creating opportunities for the company's wafer fabrication equipment, while rising manufacturing complexity supports demand for differentiated process technologies.

Applied Materials is expanding its technology portfolio to capitalize on these opportunities. Its Centris Spectral SiN ALD system supports advanced logic manufacturing, while enhanced Centura Prime epitaxy and Producer Avila 2 PECVD systems target DRAM performance and higher-layer-count high-bandwidth memory.

Beyond revenue growth, Semiconductor Systems is strengthening Applied Materials' profitability. Its non-GAAP gross margin increased to 55.4% in the third quarter from 53.5% a year earlier. The operating margin expanded to 38% from 33.2%, reflecting the value of its technology portfolio and operating leverage.

AMAT anticipates fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 Semiconductor Systems revenues to be approximately $7.9 billion, suggesting 62% year-over-year growth. The outlook indicates that demand across leading-edge logic, DRAM and advanced packaging could sustain strong near-term momentum.

How Competitors Fare Against AMAT

Applied Materials faces competition from Lam Research (LRCX), KLA Corporation (KLAC) and other semiconductor equipment suppliers, although their primary areas of specialization differ. Lam Research secured multiple critical etch wins at a major DRAM manufacturer with its new Akara etch system, which supports 3D DRAM architectures. This was supported by LRCX's customer investments in DDR5, LPDDR5 and high-bandwidth memory.

Lam Research's Aether dry-resist technology was recently selected as the production tool of record for a leading DRAM customer, securing a foothold in this high-growth segment. Although KLA does not compete directly with AMAT across its entire Semiconductor Systems portfolio, both companies can benefit from rising investment in advanced logic, high-bandwidth memory and advanced packaging.

Applied Materials shares have climbed 59.1% year to date, outperforming the Zacks Computer and Technology sector and the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry's appreciation of 15.9% and 18%, respectively.

news.Title: MRVL Taps Into AI Infrastructure Growth: What's Next for Investors?
news.Content:
Marvell Technology MRVL is benefiting from rising demand for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, with its custom silicon, optical interconnect and switching solutions driving strong data center growth. The company's expanding partnerships and broader product portfolio are strengthening its position in next-generation AI systems. However, margin pressures, customer concentration and a premium valuation remain key considerations for investors.

Marvell's second-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues increased 36.5% year over year to $2.74 billion, driven by hyperscalers, as they continued investing in AI infrastructure. Demand for 800G optical digital signal processors (DSPs) remained strong, while next-generation 1.6T products ramped up rapidly. Meanwhile, scale-out switching revenues are expected to more than double in fiscal 2027, supported by growing adoption of its 51.2T switching products.

Marvell expects its custom silicon business to accelerate in the second half of fiscal 2027, with revenues projected to more than double year over year in fiscal 2028. Demand for custom accelerators and related connectivity solutions is creating opportunities as hyperscalers develop increasingly sophisticated AI systems.

The company is also expanding its networking capabilities across scale-up, scale-out and scale-across architectures. Its strategic partnership with NVIDIA strengthens its participation in next-generation AI infrastructure through NVLink Fusion integration, optics and related connectivity technologies. Recent acquisitions of Celestial AI and XConn Technologies further broaden its technology portfolio.

How Competitors Fare Against MRVL

In the data center market, MRVL faces stiff competition from Broadcom AVGO and Advanced Micro Devices AMD.

Broadcom is a leader in the domain of custom silicon solutions for data centers. Broadcom's advanced 3.5D XDSiP packaging platform is critical to ensure the performance and efficiency of custom AI XPUs. Broadcom's relationships with leading hyperscale and frontier AI customers give it direct insight into workload requirements and help shape differentiated accelerators. The company continues to work with six core XPU customers across multiyear programs.

Advanced Micro Devices is another established player in the custom silicon solutions and AI accelerator market. Advanced Micro Devices offers semi-custom SoCs and Instinct Accelerators to power data centers. AMD is broadening its data center AI opportunity from Instinct accelerators to the Helios rack-scale platform. In the second quarter of 2026, Data Center revenues rose 107% year over year to $6.7 billion, while Instinct sales more than doubled.

Story Continues

MRVL's Price Performance, Valuation and Estimates

Marvell Technology shares have rallied 188.1% year to date, outperforming the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry and Zacks Computer and Technology sector's appreciation of 16% and 18%, respectively.

news.Title: Can Strong Momentum in LoRa Boost Semtech's Long-Term Growth?
news.Content:
Semtech Corporation SMTC is seeing strong growth in its LoRa business as demand increases across industrial, commercial and consumer applications. LoRa-enabled net sales reached a record $58 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2027, up 31% sequentially and 58% year over year. Growth reflects wider adoption of LoRa across different applications, including smart homes, security systems and industrial monitoring. Management expects the business to maintain its momentum, with LoRa revenues projected to grow about 15% sequentially and 65% year over year in the third quarter of fiscal 2027.

Semtech is expanding its LoRa portfolio to address more applications. Its LoRa Gen 4 platform supports higher data speeds while maintaining low power consumption and long-range connectivity. These features can support new uses in smart homes, security and industrial applications. For example, LoRa-enabled sensors can help monitor industrial equipment and support predictive maintenance. In public safety, the technology can also enable sensors to transmit audio for AI-based verification instead of sending simple alerts.

Amazon Sidewalk is another potential growth driver for Semtech's LoRa business. Following Ring's launch of a new range of LoRa-based sensors in the United States, Amazon Sidewalk is expanding internationally, starting with Canada and Mexico, while Europe, Australia and Japan are expected to follow. This expansion could help increase the use of LoRa-based devices in consumer applications through Amazon's network. Meanwhile, LoRa Plus is gaining traction in smart home and security markets, broadening the company's opportunities beyond traditional industrial and commercial use cases.

Strong momentum in LoRaWAN, LoRa Plus and Amazon Sidewalk can also support SMTC's future growth. Management expects LoRa revenues to grow at a rate above its previous 20% benchmark, supported by demand across these applications. With record revenues, new use cases and expanding distribution through Amazon Sidewalk, LoRa could become an increasingly important contributor to Semtech's overall growth.

How Competitors Fare Against SMTC

Semtech faces competition from Texas Instruments TXN and NXP Semiconductors NXPI across the broader industrial and Internet of Things (IoT) markets.

Texas Instruments offers Sub-1 GHz wireless microcontrollers and transceivers designed for applications such as smart meters, building automation and industrial sensors. These products provide long-range connectivity while using little power, making them an alternative for certain applications served by Semtech's LoRa technology. In the third quarter of 2026, TXN's revenues rose 28% year over year to $6.1 billion, while industrial revenues grew more than 40%. The company is expanding manufacturing capacity to support rising customer demand. These investments and its broad wireless product portfolio strengthen TXN's position in industrial and connected-device markets.

Story Continues

NXPI also offers low-power Sub-GHz wireless products for smart metering, home and building automation, asset tracking and industrial monitoring. Its OL2385 transceiver family supports multiple wireless protocols, including Sigfox and Wireless M-Bus, giving customers options for connected-device applications. NXPI's industrial and IoT business reported revenues of $755 million in the second quarter of 2026, up 38% year over year. Its newer processing products, including the i.MX, RT and MCX families, grew 40% year over year, reflecting strong demand for its industrial and IoT portfolio.

SMTC's Price Performance, Valuation & Estimates

Shares of SMTC have jumped 92.2% in the year-to-date period compared with the Zacks Semiconductor - Analog and Mixed industry's return of 38.4%.

news.Title: TXN Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Strong Analog, Data Center Demand
news.Content:
Texas Instruments Incorporated TXN reported third-quarter 2026 earnings of $2.62 per share, which increased 77% year over year. The bottom line beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 9.2%.

TXN posted revenues of $6.06 billion, which rose 28% from the year-ago quarter. The top line surpassed the consensus mark by 2.2%, driven by broad-based growth across industrial, automotive and data center markets. Data center revenues surged approximately 95% year over year.

TXN's Segment Mix Reflects Broad-Based Growth

Texas Instruments' third-quarter results reflected strong growth across its Analog and Embedded Processing segments, supported by improving demand conditions across key end markets.

Analog revenues came in at $4.91 billion (81.1% of total revenues), which grew 32% from the year-ago quarter. The figure came above our model estimate of $4.79 billion. The segment's operating profit increased 69% year over year to $2.51 billion, benefiting from stronger demand and improving manufacturing utilization.

Texas Instruments Incorporated Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Texas Instruments Incorporated price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Texas Instruments Incorporated Quote

Embedded Processing revenues totaled $858 million (14.2% of total revenues), reflecting 21% year-over-year growth. The figure surpassed our model estimate of $823.1 million. The segment's operating profit surged 110% to $227 million, supported by improving profitability as the business continued its cyclical recovery.

The Other segment generated $286 million in revenues (4.7% of total revenues), declining 6% from the prior-year quarter. The figure missed our model estimate of $293.9 million. The segment's operating profit increased 106% to $142 million.

Texas Instruments Benefits From End-Market Momentum

Industrial revenues increased more than 40% year over year and approximately 10% sequentially, supported by demand across aerospace and defense, energy infrastructure, test and measurement, and robotics.

Automotive revenues grew at a mid-teens percentage rate year over year and approximately 10% sequentially. Management highlighted improving customer demand, particularly in China and the United States, alongside increasing semiconductor content in hybrid electric and powertrain systems.

Data center revenues increased approximately 20% sequentially, reflecting sustained investments in computing infrastructure. Personal electronics revenues remained approximately flat year over year but increased at an upper-single-digit rate sequentially. Communications equipment revenues grew both year over year and sequentially.

Story Continues

TXN's Margins Expand on Higher Revenues

Texas Instruments' gross profit increased 42.7% year over year to $3.89 billion. Gross margin expanded approximately 680 basis points (bps) year over year to 64.2%, benefiting primarily from higher revenues, alongside favorable pricing, manufacturing loadings and product mix.

Selling, general and administrative expenses increased 4.2% year over year to $476 million. As a percentage of revenues, SG&A expenses contracted approximately 180 bps to 7.9%.

Research and development expenses increased 2.3% year over year to $530 million. As a percentage of revenues, R&D expenses declined approximately 220 bps to 8.8%.

Operating profit surged 72.8% year over year to $2.87 billion. Operating margin expanded approximately 1,240 bps to 47.5%.

Texas Instruments Strengthens Its Manufacturing Position

Texas Instruments continued expanding manufacturing capacity to support rising semiconductor demand. Management highlighted its investments in 300mm wafer manufacturing and assembly and test operations as key competitive advantages.

The company is ramping manufacturing operations in Malaysia while expanding capacity at its Lehi facilities. Management also highlighted improving Analog pricing during the second half of 2026, supported by stronger demand and tighter industry supply conditions.

Capital expenditure plans for 2026 remain between $2 billion and $3 billion, with spending potentially approaching the higher end depending on equipment delivery schedules.

TXN's Cash Generation Supports Shareholder Returns

As of Sept. 30, 2026, cash and short-term investments totaled $8.14 billion. Long-term debt stood at $12.91 billion, while the current portion of long-term debt was $650 million.

Texas Instruments generated operating cash flow of $3.42 billion during the quarter, while capital expenditures totaled $463 million. Quarterly free cash flow reached $2.96 billion.

During the quarter, TXN repurchased shares worth $48 million and paid $1.30 billion in dividends. The company also repaid $500 million in debt.

Trailing 12-month free cash flow increased 249% year over year to $8.42 billion. Management announced a 7% dividend increase to $1.52 per share, marking its 23rd consecutive annual dividend increase.

Texas Instruments Provides Q4 2026 Guidance

Management expects fourth-quarter 2026 revenues between $5.80 billion and $6.30 billion, with a midpoint of $6.05 billion.

Texas Instruments anticipates earnings per share between $2.45 and $2.79. The company expects an effective tax rate of approximately 13% for the fourth quarter and 13-14% for 2027.

Management expects industrial, automotive and data center demand to support fourth-quarter performance. Continued strength in data center infrastructure investments and industrial recovery underpins the company's outlook, while manufacturing capacity expansion remains a key operational priority.

Zacks Rank and Other Stocks to Consider

Currently, TXN carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy).

Some other top-ranked stocks in the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector are Analog Devices ADI , Applied Materials AMAT and Cisco Systems CSCO , each carrying a Zacks Rank #2 at present. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Shares of Analog Devices have rallied 49.7% year to date. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for ADI's fiscal 2026 earnings is pegged at $13 per share, up by 4 cents over the past seven days, indicating an increase of 66.9% year over year.

Shares of Applied Materials have jumped 59.1% year to date. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for AMAT's fiscal 2026 earnings is pegged at $12.79 per share, unchanged over the past 30 days, indicating a rise of 35.8% year over year.

Cisco Systems shares have surged 39.2% year to date. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for CSCO's fiscal 2027 earnings is pegged at $5.11 per share, unchanged over the past 30 days, indicating an increase of 18% year over year.

news.Title: Monolithic Power (MPWR) Reports Next Week: Wall Street Expects Earnings Growth
news.Content:
Monolithic Power (MPWR) is expected to deliver a year-over-year increase in earnings on higher revenues when it reports results for the quarter ended September 2026. This widely-known consensus outlook gives a good sense of the company's earnings picture, but how the actual results compare to these estimates is a powerful factor that could impact its near-term stock price.

The stock might move higher if these key numbers top expectations in the upcoming earnings report, which is expected to be released on October 29. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.

While the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call, it's worth handicapping the probability of a positive EPS surprise.

Zacks Consensus Estimate

This chipmaker is expected to post quarterly earnings of $7.80 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +64.9%.

Revenues are expected to be $1.16 billion, up 57.5% from the year-ago quarter.

Estimate Revisions Trend

The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 4.33% higher over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.

Investors should keep in mind that the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts may not always get reflected in the aggregate change.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. This insight is at the core of our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction).

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.

A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.

Story Continues

Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).

How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for Monolithic?

For Monolithic, the Most Accurate Estimate is higher than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that analysts have recently become bullish on the company's earnings prospects. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of +1.35%.

On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #2.

So, this combination indicates that Monolithic will most likely beat the consensus EPS estimate.

Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue?

While calculating estimates for a company's future earnings, analysts often consider to what extent it has been able to match past consensus estimates. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number.

For the last reported quarter, it was expected that Monolithic would post earnings of $5.88 per share when it actually produced earnings of $6.50, delivering a surprise of +10.54%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates four times.

Bottom Line

An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss.

That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. This is why it's worth checking a company's Earnings ESP and Zacks Rank ahead of its quarterly release. Make sure to utilize our Earnings ESP Filter to uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they've reported.

Monolithic appears a compelling earnings-beat candidate. However, investors should pay attention to other factors too for betting on this stock or staying away from it ahead of its earnings release.

Expected Results of an Industry Player

Another stock from the Zacks Semiconductor - Analog and Mixed industry, NXP Semiconductors (NXPI), is soon expected to post earnings of $4.14 per share for the quarter ended September 2026. This estimate indicates a year-over-year change of +33.1%. Revenues for the quarter are expected to be $3.77 billion, up 18.8% from the year-ago quarter.

The consensus EPS estimate for NXP has been revised 0.5% higher over the last 30 days to the current level. However, a lower Most Accurate Estimate has resulted in an Earnings ESP of -0.27%.

When combined with a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy), this Earnings ESP makes it difficult to conclusively predict that NXP will beat the consensus EPS estimate. Over the last four quarters, the company surpassed consensus EPS estimates three times.

news.Title: U.S. Futures Plunge as Chip Stocks Sink After Tech Earnings, Oil Rises
news.Content:
December S&P 500 E-Mini futures (ESZ26) are down -1.03%, and December Nasdaq 100 E-Mini futures (NQZ26) are down -1.78% this morning as the first round of Big Tech earnings reignited concerns about the sustainability of the AI trade, sparking a selloff in chipmakers and other AI-related stocks.

Meta Platforms (META) raised the lower end of its full-year capital expenditure guidance while leaving the upper end unchanged and offered no specific details on its 2027 spending plans beyond saying it would continue "investing aggressively." Quilter Cheviot's Ben Barringer said the absence of a substantial increase means "there's not much there for the AI CapEx trade." Meanwhile, Tesla (TSLA) cut its full-year capital spending forecast. Taken together, these developments reignited concerns about AI investments, sending chipmakers and AI infrastructure stocks sharply lower in pre-market trading. Marvell Technology (MRVL), Intel (INTC), and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) each fell -4% or more.

More News from Barchart

'No Question Tesla's Going to Merge With SpaceX' — Kevin O'Leary Says If You Own Tesla Stock, You'll Own the New Company After Flying Roadster Demo

Jensen Huang Says the Next Wave of AI Is Physical. Forget Nvidia and Tesla, I'd Bet on These 2 Mid-Cap Stocks Instead.

AST SpaceMobile Stock Gets a New Catalyst. Wall Street Sees 93% Upside.

Get exclusive insights with the FREE Barchart Brief newsletter. Subscribe now for quick, incisive midday market analysis you won't find anywhere else.

Adding to the downbeat mood, WTI crude climbed more than +2% on Thursday after deadly attacks in Saudi Arabia raised concerns that escalating Middle East tensions could disrupt oil supplies. A drone attack on Saudi Aramco's Shaybah field left two people dead but did not disrupt operations, while a separate strike on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam killed one person. The attacks heightened fears that the U.S. and Israel could resume direct military action against Iran. The New York Times reported that the U.S. and Israeli militaries have drawn up detailed plans for renewed strikes on Iran after the U.S. midterm elections.

Treasuries climbed across the curve as the selloff in AI-related stocks prompted investors to seek refuge in safe-haven assets. The 10-year T-note yield fell eight basis points to 5.05%.

Investors are now awaiting a new wave of corporate earnings reports.

In yesterday's trading session, Wall Street's three main equity benchmarks ended in the green, buoyed by strong results from SpaceX and Super Micro. SpaceX (SPCX) climbed over +7% and was the top percentage gainer in the Nasdaq 100 after the rocket and AI company reported upbeat Q3 results, while CEO Elon Musk outlined an ambitious 2027 ARR forecast and endorsed the prospect of a merger with Tesla. Also, Super Micro Computer (SMCI) surged more than +9% and was among the top percentage gainers in the S&P 500 after the AI server maker reported preliminary Q1 revenue and gross margins above its previous guidance. In addition, chip and AI infrastructure stocks advanced as strong results from SpaceX and Super Micro boosted sentiment toward the AI trade, with Western Digital (WDC) and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) gaining more than +3%. On the bearish side, Netflix (NFLX) slid over -5% after the streaming giant issued below-consensus Q4 guidance.

Story Continues

Third-quarter corporate earnings season is in full swing, with investors awaiting results from major companies today, including Western Digital (WDC), Procter & Gamble (PG), Union Pacific (UNP), Lockheed Martin (LMT), and Bloom Energy (BE). According to Bloomberg Intelligence, S&P 500 companies are expected to post an average +25% jump in third-quarter earnings from a year earlier.

On the economic front, investors will be watching U.S. initial jobless claims data, set to be released in a couple of hours. Economists expect applications for U.S. unemployment benefits to come in at 200K in the week ended Oct. 17, compared with 199K in the prior week.

The Conference Board Leading Economic Index for the U.S. will also be released today. Economists expect the September figure to fall -0.1% m/m, matching the drop recorded in August.

U.S. rate futures are currently pricing in an 87.3% probability of no rate change and a 12.7% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike at the upcoming monetary policy meeting.

In the bond market, the yield on the benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury note is at 5.05%, down -1.56%.

The Euro Stoxx 50 Index is down -1.77% this morning, pressured by declines in heavyweight banking, technology, and luxury stocks on a busy day for earnings. Rising oil prices amid escalating tensions in the Middle East further dampened sentiment. Bank stocks led the declines on Thursday as turbulence in the Eurozone bond market weighed on the sector. Tech stocks also sank as mixed earnings results from major U.S. tech companies failed to sustain the rebound in the AI trade. In addition, luxury stocks slumped, weighed down by a slide of more than -7% in Birkin bag maker Hermes (RMS.FP) after it posted weaker-than-expected Q3 revenue. Data released on Thursday showed that France's manufacturing business climate index climbed in October to its highest level since July 2022. Meanwhile, French government bond yields jumped on Thursday amid growing investor concerns over France's weakening fiscal position and mounting debt load, while German bunds gained on safe-haven demand. In other corporate news, Nestle (NESN.Z.IX) rose over +1% after the Swiss packaged-food group reported better-than-expected Q3 organic sales growth.

France's Business Survey was released today.

The French October Business Survey came in at 105, stronger than expectations of 101.

Asian stock markets today closed in the red. China's Shanghai Composite Index ($CHSC) closed down -1.48%, and Japan's Nikkei 225 Stock Index ($NKY) closed down -2.65%.

China's Shanghai Composite Index closed lower today, hitting its lowest level in more than a year as a selloff in technology stocks and waning hopes for additional economic stimulus weighed on sentiment. Tech shares tumbled on Thursday as growing concerns about the profitability of the nation's AI companies sparked another wave of selling. Investor confidence was also undermined by diminishing hopes for substantial stimulus from Beijing following China's relatively strong Q3 GDP data. While policymakers have taken steps to ease selling pressure and stabilize the equity market, analysts warned that those measures alone may not be enough to reverse the downturn. The selloff in mainland Chinese stocks has wiped out $2.4 trillion in market capitalization since a recent peak, according to Bloomberg-compiled data. "Investor sentiment remains very poor for China's onshore and offshore markets, and without new policy or tech catalysts, this kind of volatile, directionless environment may persist into early 2027," said Homin Lee at Lombard Odier. Meanwhile, Chinese President Xi Jinping called for meaningful improvements in economic quality and reasonable quantitative growth in a speech on Thursday, according to Xinhua. "We must resolutely promote high-quality development and continuously meet the people's ever-growing needs for a better life," Xi said. Elsewhere, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday that Chinese AI startup DeepSeek raised roughly 100 billion yuan ($14.98 billion) in its latest funding round. In corporate news, Alibaba Group sank over -6% in Hong Kong after Chinese authorities summoned e-commerce companies and urged stricter product-quality standards.

Japan's Nikkei 225 Stock Index closed sharply lower today as U.S. megacap earnings failed to sustain the rebound in the AI trade. Rising oil prices amid escalating Middle East tensions also weighed on sentiment. Chip-related stocks cratered on Thursday, erasing the previous session's gains as investors grew increasingly concerned about the outlook for AI spending. The selloff followed Tesla's decision to lower its full-year capex forecast. "[The market] frets when companies ramp spending, and it frets when they pull it back, as we've just seen with Tesla. In this environment, it's almost impossible to get the balance right," said Tim Waterer at KCM Trade. The Nikkei closed below the 63,000 mark for the first time since Sept. 14. Meanwhile, Japanese government bonds climbed on Thursday, pushing yields to multi-week lows as the equity selloff prompted investors to seek refuge in safe-haven assets. In other news, Japan's largest labor union federation, Rengo, said it will seek wage increases of at least 5% during the annual spring wage negotiations between the country's unions and employers, known as shunto. Elsewhere, foreign investors sold a net 66.5 billion yen worth of Japanese stocks in the week ended Oct. 17, reversing course after substantial net purchases of 3.55 trillion yen the previous week, according to Ministry of Finance data. Market participants are now turning their attention to Japan's September national core CPI, preliminary October PMIs, and the Bank of Japan's Financial System Report, all due on Friday. The Nikkei Volatility Index, which takes into account the implied volatility of Nikkei 225 options, closed up +16.60% at 35.97.

Pre-Market U.S. Stock Movers

Tesla (TSLA) sank nearly -5% in pre-market trading after the EV maker cut its full-year capital spending forecast.

Meta Platforms (META) dropped more than -2% in pre-market trading despite reporting record Q3 revenue that topped expectations, as its shares were caught up in the broader AI selloff.

Other Magnificent Seven stocks declined amid risk-off sentiment, with Alphabet (GOOGL) and Amazon.com (AMZN) falling over -2%.

Chip and AI infrastructure stocks slid in pre-market trading after earnings from Tesla and Meta Platforms reignited concerns about the sustainability of AI spending. Marvell Technology (MRVL), Intel (INTC), and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) each fell -4% or more.

Lam Research (LRCX) slumped about -8% in pre-market trading after the semiconductor capital equipment company issued soft FQ2 guidance.

news.Title: 聯電攜手愛普科技推進AI與高效能運算系統電源解決方案
news.Content:
財經中心/綜合報導

聯華電子與愛普科技於今(22)日共同宣布展開技術與製造合作，推進AI與高效能運算(HPC)系統的供電解決方案。此次合作結合聯電的深溝槽電容(Deep Trench Capacitor, DTC)製程技術與可擴充的晶圓製造能力，以及愛普科技的矽電容設計與系統層級整合技術，共同因應下一代資料中心在電源效率方面的挑戰。

隨著AI運算工作負載快速成長，運算系統對電源傳輸的要求日益提高，推動資料中心的電源架構從傳統將穩壓元件配置於電路板上，逐步轉向將電容直接嵌入中介層(Interposer)或基板中。此創新架構可縮短電源傳輸路徑、提升電源完整性(Power Integrity)，並支援先進封裝內更有效率的電壓調節。

聯電與愛普科技的合作已於2026年第三季達成重要里程碑，愛普科技S-SiCapTM Gen2D分離式矽電容設計已完成投片及初步功能驗證。下一階段將針對封裝基板中的電容進行完整的系統級效能與可靠度測試，目標是支援不同的電容量與工作電壓需求。雙方也正探討將合作拓展至其他包括矽中介層嵌入式電容及基板底面電容的產品線，以因應多元的系統設計需求。

聯電資深副總經理洪圭鈞表示：「AI 與 HPC 的成長正推動電源傳輸架構根本性的轉變，從電路板層級的供電，逐步走向晶片層級的垂直電源整合。聯電提供完整的供電解決方案，包括DTC技術，可將高密度電容配置於更靠近運算晶片的位置，以達到更穩定晶片供電效果。聯電透過與愛普科技合作，正致力將可擴充的解決方案推向市場，以克服 AI 基礎設施持續演進所帶來的關鍵供電瓶頸。」

愛普科技總經理洪志勳表示：「採用 DTC 技術的客製化S-SiCapTM 產品成功完成投片及初步晶圓驗證，是展現愛普科技S-SiCapTM 設計彈性與可製造性的重要里程碑。透過與聯電的合作，我們為客戶提供從產品設計到晶圓製造的一站式解決方案。」

聯電的供電解決方案藍圖涵蓋可應用於不同系統架構的分離式與嵌入式矽電容，並延伸至內部電壓調節器等主動元件。聯電亦運用其先進封裝能力，實現更高密度的電源元件整合，以滿足下世代資料中心對更高電壓與電容量的需求。同時，聯電持續投資擴充製造產能，以支援電源與異質整合解決方案。

中國A股主要指數今(22)日全面收黑，上證指數失守3700點，收於3658.03點，下跌1.48%，日K連二黑；深證成指收於11357.32點，下跌2.96%；創業板指收於2576.90點，下跌4.37%；科創50收於1305.87點，下跌2.78%。盤勢開低走低，尾盤未能明顯修復，整體情緒偏弱。

兩市成交量1兆5,287億元(人民幣,下同)，較前一交易日量增約7%。盤面上，成長與科技權重成為壓力核心，創業板指跌幅最大，顯示成長型資產承壓明顯；科創50同步回落，亦反映科技成長類族群賣壓沉重，市場在收盤前仍未見有效止跌訊號。

AI硬體鏈調整最為明顯，新易盛、中際旭創、天孚通信等權重股走弱，光通信、CPO、PCB、元件、記憶體晶片與先進封裝等普遍下挫；通訊、電子、傳媒等類股跌幅居前，科技相關概念同步承壓。電池產業鏈同樣拖累指數表現，寧德時代走勢疲弱，新能源車與電池相關標的同步偏弱，對創業板指形成明顯壓力。
